items.stem: Why does availability often take priority over confidentiality in OT environments?

options.text: Interrupting physical processes can cause safety and production harm
options.rationale: Correct: OT controls physical processes where downtime can be dangerous.

options.text: Because OT data is never sensitive
options.rationale: OT can hold sensitive data; the priority reflects physical risk.

options.text: Because confidentiality is impossible in OT
options.rationale: Confidentiality still matters; it is simply often outranked by availability.

options.text: Because OT systems have no users
options.rationale: OT systems have operators; the point is physical-process risk.

items.explanation: Correct: OT runs physical processes where loss of availability can harm safety.

items.stem: Which TWO practices suit OT security? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Segmenting the plant network from the corporate network
options.rationale: Correct: segmentation limits exposure to the control environment.

options.text: Using passive monitoring that does not disrupt controllers
options.rationale: Correct: passive monitoring avoids destabilising sensitive devices.

options.text: Running aggressive active scans on live controllers
options.rationale: Active scans can crash fragile OT devices.
Unmonitored standing access is a major OT risk.

items.explanation: Correct: segmentation and passive monitoring both suit OT constraints.

items.stem: Why is unauthenticated industrial protocol traffic a concern?

options.text: Commands can be forged or altered because the protocol does not verify the sender
options.rationale: Correct: lack of authentication lets attackers issue or tamper with commands.

options.text: Because the protocol encrypts everything by default
options.rationale: Many industrial protocols lack both authentication and encryption.

options.text: Because it makes devices run faster
options.rationale: Speed is unrelated to the authentication concern.

options.text: Because it only affects office email
options.rationale: The concern is control commands, not email.

items.explanation: Correct: without authentication, control commands can be forged or altered.
